symptom: `mxcli describe rule M.Rule_X` prints "Unknown type: rule" and bare `mxcli describe M.Rule_X` says no describable document is found, while `mxcli -c "describe rule M.Rule_X"` works
cause: Same drift as #1347: describeMDLCommand had no RULE case, and the auto-detect maps (catalog ObjectType RULE, unit $Type Microflows$Rule) omitted rules — the unit map even said so on purpose, a leftover from before the executor could describe rules
fix: Added RULE -> DESCRIBE RULE, objectTypeToDescribe[RULE] and unitTypeToDescribe[Microflows$Rule] = rule, plus the help and Valid-types lines
insight: Second instance of the subcommand's hand-kept type list lagging the DESCRIBE grammar. The executor's own bare-DESCRIBE map (mdl/executor/describe_auto.go objectTypeToDescribeKind) already had RULE — diffing that map's keys against cmd/mxcli's objectTypeToDescribe is the quickest way to find the next missing doctype. The 'not a rule in this project' refusal in the same report is a downstream effect, not a describe bug.
